<reason>A better established the proposition’s comparison: transferable ownership reproduces opportunity advantages across generations without requiring renewed earnings. A directly addressed gifts, trust valuation, and business liquidity. B raised meaningful timing and enforcement objections, but repeatedly treated a gift-inclusive proposal as funeral-only and conflated investment income generated by dynastic assets with the motion’s comparison to most high earners. B also misleadingly generalized A’s conditional concession that transfers below the exemption might yield no tax.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s strongest response distinguished receiving legal title from receiving dynastic advantages, then showed that a middle-aged recipient’s inheritance can finance the next generation’s childhood. This substantially defeated B’s central claim that inheritance taxation necessarily arrives after the opportunity race is over.</best_rebuttal>
